title: Vision-guided navigation on a microcontroller robot
summary: A single-camera mobile robot that tracks moving targets, judges obstacle distance from monocular geometry, and explores an unknown grid, with all reasoning happening on the microcontroller itself and no external computer or localization.

sections.heading: The problem
body: Give a small wheeled robot everything it needs to navigate using nothing but a single onboard camera and a microcontroller: no GPS, no external localization, no offboard compute. That splits into three connected problems.
list: Track a moving visual target in closed loop.
Judge how far away an obstacle is from a single 2D image, with no depth sensor.
Build up a map of an unknown space from nothing but local visual landmarks.

sections.heading: Approach
list: A PID controller keeps the pan servo locked onto a coloured blob, tuned by physically running the robot against a monitor playing a moving target at swept frequencies (0.03-2.8 Hz) and swept gains, logging error and angle at every step.

Obstacle distance comes from a single-camera trick: calibrate once against a reference object of known real-world size, then convert an obstacle's apparent size and position into a real distance and bearing using the law of cosines, accounting for the blind zone directly beneath the camera's field of view.
The exploration and mapping logic builds an internal grid incrementally from blob-based landmarks. It went through six full rewrites.

sections.heading: Result
body: All three subsystems run on the microcontroller itself, from closed-loop tracking through monocular distance estimation to incremental mapping.
list: Tracking was tuned from logged sweep data rather than by feel. Raising the proportional gain from 0.5 to 1.2 cut tracking error by 54% and nearly tripled the rate at which the servo reversed direction, putting the responsiveness and smoothness trade-off in measured terms.
Calibration succeeded in 17 of 28 runs, with the remainder traced to the robot's physical angle against the target display restricting the pan servo's available sweep.
The mapping logic was rebuilt six times, each version kept as its own file, giving a full record of how the exploration strategy converged.

sections.heading: Further work
list: Calibration assumes an unobstructed pan sweep relative to the target, so a setup-independent routine would make it more robust.
Distance estimation is calibrated against a reference object of known real-world size. Extending it to arbitrary obstacles needs a second view or a learned depth prior.
